import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 238

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)
-/

open scoped Topology
open Set Filter Real

namespace Erdos238

/--
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (c₁ > 0) (c₂ > 0), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry

/--
It is well-known that the conjecture above is true when `c₁` is sufficiently small.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238.variants.small_c1 : ∀ c₂ > 0, ∀ᶠ c₁ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry


end Erdos238

reformulations.difference: Lean infers c₂ : ℕ and checks the k−1 adjacent prime gaps, whereas the source allows arbitrary positive constants and requires separation between every two distinct primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any positive real threshold C, choose a positive natural n > C. A block whose gaps exceed n also has gaps exceeding C; conversely, the real-threshold statement specializes to natural thresholds. Nat.nth Nat.Prime enumerates all primes strictly increasingly, so the specified f has exactly k distinct consecutive primes. Every nonadjacent difference is at least an intervening adjacent gap, and adjacent pairs are among all pairs. The exact raw Lean statement was proved equivalent to the real-threshold, all-pairs formulation in Review238.raw_main_equivalence.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses sufficiently small positive c₁ using eventuality in 𝓝[>] 0, and again uses natural c₂ and adjacent gaps.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The right-hand neighborhood condition is equivalent to existence of δ > 0 such that every 0 < c₁ < δ satisfies the eventual-in-x block condition. Because c₂ is quantified first, δ may depend on c₂, while the eventual x cutoff may depend on both constants, exactly as the source requires. Cofinality of natural thresholds and equivalence of adjacent and pairwise separation apply as above. Review238.raw_small_equivalence proves the full equivalence with explicit real constants, δ, and x cutoffs.

review.notes: Both declarations match the source, including their open/solved categories. Independent equivalence proofs and boundary tests compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. Tests cover initial prime gaps, injectivity and consecutiveness of the prime enumeration, nontriviality of both filters, and the fact that fixed positive c₁ forces k beyond every fixed bound as x grows, preventing empty/singleton witnesses from trivializing the claims.
